title: Add read-only host check for records-branch and main rules
summary: Add a read-only check in athena-core that queries the host (via the existing gh runner) for protection on athena/records (force-pushes forbidden, deletion forbidden) and on main (require up-to-date branches), and reports each of the three as in force or not. Audience: Sri, who must configure these host rules before the records cutover. Tests parse fixture replies; no host setting is changed.

defaults_applied.how: Module has passing tests; clippy and fmt clean.
Criteria check reported states from fixture replies, not mere existence.
One focused module and its tests.
Doc comments written for outside readers.
Behavior criteria runnable via cargo test/clippy/fmt.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Host is GitHub; the check uses the branch-protection REST endpoint (allow_force_pushes, allow_deletions, required_status_checks.strict) via the existing Runner/gh api path.
Rulesets (rather than classic branch protection) may also express these rules; the check handles classic protection and, if cheap, the rules/branches endpoint, otherwise notes the limit.
Only a library function and tests are required; wiring into a CLI command is optional and omitted unless a natural hook exists.
HostOperation (a records schema enum) is not extended, to avoid changing the records format.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests feed fixture host replies (protection present, protection absent/404 'Branch not protected', and partial) and assert each of the three rules (no force-push and no deletion on athena/records; up-to-date required on main) is reported as in force or not as the fixture dictates.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean; `cargo test` passes for the workspace.
The check issues only read requests (GET); a test with a recording fake runner asserts no call uses a non-GET method or passes fields, so no host setting is changed.
A host error other than 'not protected' (e.g. 403 or 5xx) is reported as unknown/error, not as 'not in force' and not as success; a test covers it.
The report names each rule and its state in plain text a reader can act on, e.g. 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force / not in force'.
Doc comments cite D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3; the work is described as part 3 of job 1.

out_of_scope: Setting or changing any host branch rule or protection
Building the records-check status, cutover, or other records-history jobs
